prerequisites: Positive credit of Materials Science I lecture course
Positive credit of Materials Science I laboratory practice

learning_outcomes.text: Know the rules of division, classification and notatation for non-alloyed steels, alloyed steels, casts and their application
Know the basement of termo and termo-chemical treatments and their influence on steel properties
Know the types and properties of non-iron metal alloys
Be able to divide, classification and notation of non-alloyed steels, alloyed steels, casts and their application
Be able to determine the types of heat and termo-chemical treatment application and theit influence on steel properties
Be able to determine the types and properties of non-iron metal alloys
Information retrieval and their critical analyse
Observance of custom and rules binding at academic environment

syllabus_topics: Cast irons. Grafitisation. Modification of cast irons
Types of graphite and metall matrix of cast irons. Classification and natation rules of cast irons.
Phase transformation in steels during heating
Phase transformation in steels during cooling
Basic types of annealing. Hardening and tempering of steel
TTT diagrams. Hardenability. Supersaturation and ageing
Surface treatment of steel, surface hardening, carburizing and nitriding
Influence of alloying elements on the steel phase transformation
General classification and notation rules for non-alloed steels
Structures, properties and notation rules for alloed steels
Alloyed structural steels. Weldability
Alloyed tool steels.
Steels with special properties: corrosion resistant steels, creep and heat resistant steels, maraging steels and wear resistant steels
Copper and copper alloys
Aluminium and light metal alloys
Microstructures of steels and cast steels on the basement of Fe-Fe3C system
Cast irons microstructures and properties
Influence of the heat tratment on the steels microstructure and properties
Mmicrostructures and properties of the tool steels
Microstructures of stells with special properties
Microstructures and properties of aluminium and copper alloys
Summary and supplerment of laboratory practice
Credit of laboratory practice
teaching_methods: traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides
self study - self studies and preparation for examination
self study - preparation for laboratory class
assessment_rules: For the lecture, the evaluation is based on a written-oral examination (F1). For the laboratory, the evaluation is based on an introduction test, oral answers, and a report (F1). The concluding evaluation (P) for both lecture and laboratory is equal to F1.
bibliography: M. F. Ashby- Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, vol 1 and 2
degree: Mechanical Engineering and Machine Building (I level, full-time)
